sectors.ai: Buy YELO and ELIT on momentum, but rotate into INET and AREA for sustained earnings visibility as US tech weakness filters through. Add on any pullback to 5-day moving averages.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable energy mandate and domestic content requirements are creating durable demand for local solar and geothermal players, insulating them from global rate volatility.
US climate-tech names are underperforming due to high interest rates and policy uncertainty, making selective Indonesian small-caps with strong earnings momentum more attractive.
The aggregation of niche players like GGRP and TOBA indicates a broadening of the sector beyond traditional utilities, signaling structural growth in distributed energy and biomass.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in Indonesian renewables leaders LAPD and ESSA; their outperformance vs US peers signals domestic policy tailwinds. Rotate out of US-exposed laggards like AWK. Target KEEN and POWR for near-term momentum. Maintain normal risk, add on any sector-wide pullback.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rupiah stability and falling palm-oil/plastic input costs are structurally widening FMCG gross margins, rewarding producers with pricing power and export channels.
Indonesia's middle-class consumption recovery, driven by election-year fiscal transfers and resilient rural demand, is shifting share to lower-tier brands and value-pack formats.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer models are compressing traditional trade costs, enabling smaller-cap FMCG players to scale faster and disrupt incumbents' shelf dominance.
sectors.ai: Buy selective FMCG laggards with export or commodity leverage (SRSN, OILS, AGAR) as IDX consumer momentum broadens; avoid chasing KICI/IATA one-day spikes. Position into Q3 earnings where margin recovery from input-cost deflation is visible, favoring names with volume growth over price hikes. Trim if aggregate breaks below +0.5% weekly.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Indonesia's infrastructure names are decoupling from US peers, driven by domestic capex cycle and government project disbursements, making local exposure a structural alpha source.
Small-cap movers (ASLI, LEAD) show speculative liquidity churn, but SSIA and SULI offer earnings-backed growth tied to property and steel demand from new capital projects.
The NORMAL signal suggests mean-reversion risk; favor names with confirmed order books over pure momentum plays to avoid sharp reversals.
sectors.ai: Buy ASLI and LEAD on momentum, but treat as trade-only given 20-25% spikes without earnings confirmation. Rotate into SSIA and SULI for relative value as aggregate signal stays NORMAL. Trim US-exposed names like PACK on the -0.88% divergence. Watch BALI for follow-through; if it holds +11%, add. Overall, stay selective—infrastructure is flat, so pick idiosyncratic winners, not beta.

sectors.name: Logistics

US-linked logistics names face headwinds from softer trade volumes, making domestic-focused Indonesian operators more attractive for sustained growth.
sectors.ai: Buy PPGL and SOCI on momentum, but rotate into NELY for volume-driven upside as port congestion tightens. Trim US-exposed names like WINS and SAFE on relative underperformance. Logistics aggregates stay normal, so favor high-beta movers with earnings catalysts over index-level plays.
